W2 (empirical), after E032. Tip is E027: 5.878 s, 0.7547 on seeds 0-2 (20/24/28/32 px at 15/25/30/30%, 8.75 epochs, 219 steps, batch 2000). Held-out seeds 3-12 give about 0.7526, so the real margin over the 0.753 bar is about zero.

Mechanisms, each tied to measured runs:
1. Epoch dial: about 5% of time per 0.5 epoch for 0.0-0.2 pp (E020, E023, E027). The tip is at the accuracy floor.
2. EMA (+0.97 pp, E005) and Muon (+0.66 pp, E006, confounded) are in the tip. Lookahead looks tuned. A harder pull (E025), a longer interval (E030, -0.5 pp) and late LS=0 (E032, -0.7 pp) all hurt. Time-neutral boosters have failed 5 times in a row (E025, E029, E030, E032, plus E013/E014/E022 flat).
3. Time tracks pixels and FLOPs, sublinearly on small maps. Early low-res is nearly free (E026). Dropping or shrinking the 28 px phase costs 0.3-0.5 pp (E018, E024).
4. Backward truncation (E028) saves 0.5 s, about 9%, for about -0.35 pp on seeds 0-2 against E023. Selection/skipping of work (E031: -0.7 s, -0.5 pp) also trades at roughly 0.3-0.5 pp per 0.5 s.
5. wd, LS, Muon lr, LR floor and warm-up are flat within noise. E016's 0.7607 was a lucky draw.
6. Noise: identical code is bit-identical. Any change to step count or RNG use reshuffles the 3-seed mean by about ±0.2 pp. Held-out sits about 0.2 pp below seeds 0-2. Time noise is about 0.5%.

Misses: I overpredicted time on trims (savings run 2-8% larger than modelled), and I was too optimistic on time-neutral accuracy changes (E030, E032).

Unsure: whether the freeze plus extra epochs nets positive. The freeze saves about 0.5 s and costs about 0.35 pp. Adding 0.5 epoch costs about 0.3 s and returns maybe 0.1-0.2 pp, so the stack is likely still short of the accuracy bar. Also unsure whether any bit-identical systems saving (prepare, H3.2.1) is worth more than 0.05-0.1 s.

forecasts.reason: Freeze saves ~0.5 s, +0.5 epoch adds ~0.3 s; accuracy is likely still near 0.752, so the keep gate (0.753 on seeds 0-2) is a coin flip.
Math-identical systems change; saves about 0.03-0.08 s, and accuracy should be bit-identical if the check passes.
Likely the whitening bias already stops at 3 epochs (~34% of steps), so a 20% cutoff saves a little; the effect is small and below noise.
A deeper freeze cuts more time, but it costs accuracy in the 28 px phase, and the held-out mean was already below the bar.
Fresh seeds should regress to roughly 0.7525, confirming the winner's curse and a margin near zero.
Folding BN saves a bit more on the large maps, but eval-mode BN in the frozen phase risks a small accuracy loss and adds complexity.
Diagnostic with no recipe change; it likely shows non-GEMM kernels at 30% or more of the step.
Muon is likely worth a few tenths of a pp, and removing Newton-Schulz saves about 3% time.

cruxes: Is the freeze's accuracy cost (about -0.35 pp on seeds 0-2) additive with the epoch top-up, or does the extra 0.5 epoch recover it? That decides whether the freeze plus epochs beats the tip.
Does the tip's true population mean (held-out about 0.7526) clear the 40-seed bar of 0.75 on the PCIe judge, or is more epochs needed to be safe?
Is the whitening bias already frozen before 25% of steps, and how much prepare/first-trial overhead is removable? That sets the value of the systems levers.
